title: Vocabulary: word forms and spelling for completion answers
status: Owner approved v1.0.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Lesson 3 (Listening details, spelling and word limits).
Learners know noun, verb, adjective and adverb.
Optional vocabulary lesson: use when correct ideas lose marks because of spelling, plurals or the wrong word form.

objectives.text: Choose the word form a gap needs (noun, verb, adjective, adverb; singular or plural) by reading the words around it.
Spell 20 high-frequency IELTS words correctly, including common traps (accommodation, environment, necessary).
Build word families with common suffixes (-tion, -ment, -ity, -ive, -al, -ly) to read and write more flexibly.

levels.foundation: Work with the suffix table open; spell the first ten bank words only.
levels.core: Complete all tasks with the bank closed after the word-family stage.
levels.extension: For each completion answer, name the clue word that shows the form (for example 'a' + adjective + noun).
levels.high_band: Write a word family of four forms for five bank words and use each form in a sentence.

word_bank.meaning: a place to stay (uncountable; double c, double m)
the natural world (note the n before m)
the group that rules a country (n before m)
word_bank.example: The government introduced a new law.
It is necessary to book in advance.

word_bank.meaning: how hot or cold something is
days and months need capitals and silent letters
place for books / place for experiments
nature → natural; create → creative; danger → dangerous
a gap after 'several', 'many', 'two' needs a plural
no plural: information, equipment, advice, research, furniture

stages.title: Opening challenge: right idea, lost mark
stages.student: Decide which answer would receive the mark.
stages.teacher: Learners vote; reveal comments. Stress that IELTS marks spelling and form.
stages.say: The right idea in the wrong form scores zero.
stages.check: Learners say why Learner A loses the mark.

stages.title: Word families and suffixes
stages.student: Complete a word-family table for five verbs from the bank (verb, noun, adjective, adverb).
stages.teacher: Board the suffix groups. Point out spelling changes (decide → decision, able → ability).
stages.say: The suffix tells you the job of the word.

stages.title: Which form fits the gap?
stages.student: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
stages.teacher: Six minutes; reveal and ask for the clue word each time.
stages.say: Read the words before and after the gap.

stages.title: Completion from a passage
stages.student: Complete the notes with ONE word from the passage. Copy the exact form.
stages.teacher: Eight minutes timed. Check plurals and spelling strictly.
stages.say: Copy the word exactly; check singular or plural.

stages.title: Listen and spell
stages.student: Listen once and complete the form. Spelling must be correct.
stages.teacher: Read the script once at natural speed, spelling only the names that the script spells.
stages.say: Write, then check spelling and capitals in the last minute.
stages.check: Most learners score five or more of seven.

stages.title: Spelling challenge
stages.teacher: Quick-fire; learners correct their own notebooks.
stages.say: Learn the trap, not just the word.
stages.check: Learners record their three hardest words.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the homework.
stages.say: Check every completion answer for form and spelling before you move on.
stages.check: Every learner spells five bank words correctly from memory.

blocks.mode: Controlled practice; word bank closed for core and above
blocks.instructions: Write the correct form of the word in brackets (ONE word).

items.prompt: The council made a ______ to close the road. (decide)

blocks.title: Completion from a passage
blocks.mode: Timed practice; ten minutes, no dictionary
blocks.instructions: Complete the notes. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

stimulus.title: A new sports centre
paragraphs: The town's new sports centre, which opened in March, includes a twenty-five-metre swimming pool, two gymnasiums and several outdoor courts. The building was designed to reduce energy consumption: solar panels on the roof provide around a third of its electricity, and rainwater is collected for use in the changing rooms.

Membership has exceeded expectations. Within six weeks, over two thousand residents had registered, and the centre is now considering longer opening hours at weekends. Managers say the most popular facilities are the climbing wall and the evening yoga classes, which are frequently fully booked.

Some residents have raised concerns about parking, since the car park has only eighty spaces. The council has responded by introducing a new bus route and installing secure storage for bicycles near the main entrance.

items.prompt: The centre has a pool, two ______ and outdoor courts.
The design aims to cut energy ______.
About a third of the electricity comes from solar ______.
Collected ______ is used in the changing rooms.
The most popular activities include the climbing wall and evening ______ classes.
Concerns: there are not enough ______ in the car park.
items.evidence: the car park has only eighty spaces

stimulus.title: Booking a study room
paragraphs: RECEPTIONIST: Good morning, Riverside College library. How can I help?
STUDENT: Hello, I'd like to book a study room for a group project. My surname is Whitfield, that's W-H-I-T-F-I-E-L-D.
RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. Which day would you like?
STUDENT: Wednesday, please, the fourteenth of February, in the afternoon.
RECEPTIONIST: Fine. Our rooms have whiteboards, and you can borrow a projector, but please note that food is not allowed. Will you need any equipment?
STUDENT: Just the projector, thanks. Oh, and is it necessary to bring a student card?
RECEPTIONIST: Yes, you'll need it to enter the building. The room is on the third floor, next to the laboratory.

stimulus.title: Joining a community choir
paragraphs: ORGANISER: Thanks for calling the Hillview Community Choir. Rehearsals are on Thursday evenings in the old town hall.
CALLER: Do I need any experience?
ORGANISER: No, but beginners usually attend two introductory sessions first. The membership fee covers the cost of sheet music and the hire of the hall.
CALLER: And what should I bring?

ORGANISER: Just a pencil and a bottle of water. Oh, and we're looking for volunteers to help with publicity for our spring concert, which will raise money for the local hospital. If you're interested, please contact our secretary, Mrs Coutts, that's C-O-U-T-T-S.
